newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER AND SHERINGHAM READY TO SPEARHEAD ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER AND SHERINGHAM READY TO SPEARHEAD ENGLAND.

text.p: Newcastle's Alan Shearer and Tottenham's Teddy Sheringham are likely to resume their partnership when England host Georgia in a World Cup qualifying match at Wembley on Wednesday.
The two contrasting forwards developed a fluid understanding during last June's European championship but have not played together since.
Whenever Shearer has played for England, Sheringham has either been injured or confined to the substitutes' bench.
When Sheringham played and scored against both Georgia in Tbilisi last November and against Mexico in a friendly last month, Shearer was recovering from groin operations.
Now both men are fully fit and looking to recreate what proved to be the most potent striking partnership of Euro 96.
Shearer finished the competition as top scorer with five goals while Sheringham, the perfect counter-balance to Shearer's out-and-out goalscoring, netted twice.
Despite the fact he has not played alongside Shearer since then, Sheringham's admiration for the Newcastle man has not waned.
"Without disregarding any of the players in the squad at the moment he is the best man about," the Spurs striker said.
"He is the top man. There are untold amounts of players trying to stop him scoring goals and he still keeps scoring. You can't ignore that fact and I think everyone has taken notice in the world.
"The aura around him I can only liken to Juergen Klinsmann," said Sheringham, who played alongside the German captain at Tottenham in the 1994-95 season.
"I can remember when Juergen first came over...the aura surrounding him was unbelievable and I think Alan is getting that aura around him.
"I don't think he is quite the finished player Juergen is yet, but I think he is very fast becoming that sort, even at international level."
England need a repeat of their European championship form if they are to beat Georgia on Wednesday and stay in touch with group two leaders Italy.
Glenn Hoddle's side lost 1-0 to the Italians in their last World Cup qualifier in February and were not entirely convincing in the friendly against Mexico, which they won 2-0.
But they have a virtually full-strength squad with Paul Gascoigne and left-back Stuart Pearce the only notable absentees.
Georgia enter the match still searching for their first World Cup points, having lost 1-0 in Italy and 2-0 at home to England.
But they have a number of talented players including English-based Georgi Kinkladze and Mikhail Kavelashvili and Hoddle has said he rates the side very highly.

Security will be extremely tight at Wembley in the wake of a series of Irish Republican Army bomb alerts which have disrupted the British transport network in recent weeks and caused the postponement of the Grand National horse race.
The alerts have been timed to coincide with Thursday's British general election and polling stations open less than 10 hours after the match is due to end.
Teams:
England (probable) - David Seaman, Gary Neville, Tony Adams, Gareth Southgate, Graeme Le Saux, David Beckham, David Batty, Paul Ince, Steve McManaman, Teddy Sheringham, Alan Shearer
Georgia - to be announced
